Updated September 2026
Index Work Record Stories About
Wiki/Robby Prochnow

Overview

Robby Prochnow is a technology executive with {{fact:robbie-prochnow.12-5-years}} in Fortune 500 technology businesses. At Common Ground he is CTO and the Technology & AI Architecture principal, responsible for the intelligence pillar: the AI and agentic systems that run inside the group and across its portfolio.

Prochnow is the founder of Zen Aegis, an AI transformation and intelligent automation firm. Zen Aegis builds custom intelligence infrastructure for enterprises and stays for deployment and ongoing operations rather than one-time consulting; its stated model is to build and operate inside the client organization until the results are real. The firm works with growth-stage companies, private equity portfolio operators, regulated industries, and mission-driven organizations.

Within Common Ground, the same systems Zen Aegis deploys for clients run first inside the group’s own ventures, consistent with the group’s standing claim that everything it sells, it has implemented.

Career, from his own account

Recorded September 28, 2026, from his own history and credentials record; clients are described by role, never by name.

Insight and TD SYNNEX are a reseller and a distributor, and Avnet is a distributor: he owned the Apple, Microsoft and Dell businesses inside those companies, and did not work for Apple, Microsoft or Dell.

At Insight Enterprises in Tempe, from 2013 to 2019, he built a {{fact:robbie-prochnow.usd-10m-plus}} small-business book from scratch as a field account executive, beat quota growth by {{fact:robbie-prochnow.200-pct}} as the Western Region business development manager for Apple, and then ran product management for the Microsoft business, growing Surface, software and services {{fact:robbie-prochnow.40-pct}} year over year and moving from fourth to second in market share. He was the first to architect Device as a Service and take it to market, when nobody else was selling it: the first client proof of concept was with a large college in Kansas, he raised about {{fact:robbie-prochnow.usd-1m}} from technology partners to fund the launch, and it scaled nationwide and then globally. He also won an exclusive channel partner deal for Microsoft HoloLens and founded a Mixed Reality team.

As general manager of GoDaddy’s cyber security business in Scottsdale, from 2019 to 2021, he inherited a flagship product declining {{fact:robbie-prochnow.60-pct}} year over year, stopped the decline in the first year and turned the portfolio to {{fact:robbie-prochnow.12-pct}} growth. He redesigned the security portfolio so small businesses could buy real security instead of bolt-ons, and launched Website Security Suites.

At TD SYNNEX in Phoenix, from 2021 to 2022, he ran the North America Microsoft devices, software and services business on a {{fact:robbie-prochnow.usd-1b}} P&L. He inherited it down to two people and a new hire, rebuilt the team, took it from the lowest-ranked distributor to the highest, and moved {{fact:robbie-prochnow.usd-20m}} of eight-month-aged inventory in three months. Microsoft named him Transformation Partner of the Year at Microsoft Inspire in 2021 for that business. After the Tech Data merger he was asked to lead the global Microsoft business and bring the two companies and cultures together.

At Avnet in Chandler, from 2022 to 2025, he led the global Dell partnership, centered on OEM solution design, doubled the business outside North America and took to market some of the first AI solution packages built to run on Dell servers. He then worked across about 50 suppliers on AI acceleration and cut supplier onboarding time in half.

He founded Zen Aegis in Phoenix in 2023. It began as a consulting business, became a fractional leadership firm, and is now an AI transformation partner that builds and operates custom AI agent systems inside client businesses, on the same agent infrastructure it runs itself. He has run at least 70 audits as Zen Aegis and hundreds across his career, mostly technology, plus sales, marketing, operations, and leadership and culture.

Before 2013 he worked at Wells Fargo, from teller to service manager, and at Sprint. In college he bought, repaired and resold broken computers, and ran a painting company for a summer through a College Works Painting internship: about {{fact:robbie-prochnow.usd-100k}} in revenue and the award for the most profitable painting business. He holds an MBA from Grand Canyon University and a BA in Business Legal Studies from Arizona State University. His certifications: Stack AI, Microsoft AI, n8n, and Assembly (formerly Copilot) Premium Expert; he is also in the top {{fact:robbie-prochnow.10-pct}} of Replit Agent users.

Building Common Ground's client side

Recorded October 7, 2026, from the partner mail record; clients and deal counterparties are described by role or codename, never by name.

Foyer Hall, in production

Foyer Hall is the white-label client portal Robby built: a data room, signatures, files and invoices under the firm's own brand, with an agent interface so a firm's own tools can work inside each client room. This fall Common Ground moved its first client room onto it, and real use turned up real defects. He fixed most of them the day they were reported. When Jesse sent a page of notes, eight fixes were live within about a day: sign-in links a mail scanner can no longer use up, an invite flow that asks for a name and password, branded reset pages, the firm's own logo on every screen, and two room settings, Quiet rooms and Record voice, so a room only emails the client when something needs them. When the first client invoice failed to take payment, he had it fixed and bank payment added inside two hours.

Aegis Lens

Before a client call, the usual move is to send the client a long questionnaire. Robby built a prototype so nobody has to. Aegis Lens runs inside a client's environment and collects the facts itself: identity, devices, cloud, code, software subscriptions, vendors and spend. It joins them into one picture, ranks what it finds with the evidence attached, gives any saving as a range rather than a single number, and scores how ready the business is for AI. Nothing reaches the client until a person approves it. Today it is a prototype run on sample data, and it is ready to show.

Slipstream's scoring engine

Slipstream pairs Jimmy Khounlavong's audit method with Robby's platform (see Search and AI readiness). Robby built the monitoring that re-checks a site on a schedule and flags what changed, and an automated engine that scores how a site shows up in search and AI answers. Before trusting it he ran it against Jimmy's hand audit of ten sites: it agreed {{fact:robbie-prochnow.92-8-percent}} of the time with no factual conflicts, and he explained every difference. Pointed at Common Ground's own sites, it caught drift nobody had seen.

The agent pod and how it is governed

Robby builds and runs Zen Aegis's agent team himself, and Common Ground is moving its own work onto it. His rule is that agents are poor at jobs that have to come out the same way every time, so those run as fixed workflows; agents do the reasoning, and a person approves before anything is sent. Every agent session is saved to a private, versioned record that the next session reads first, so the work does not depend on anyone's memory.

A PE-backed dental group

On a private-equity-backed dental group, Robby led the technology side. He wrote the week-by-week 90-day technology plan that the engagement's scope and rate rest on, and the data-access terms in the agreement: named, time-limited, logged accounts that can be revoked, and no change to a live system without written approval. He also proposed the business associate agreement between the firms before any patient data could move.

Inside Common Ground

Robby met the Common Ground partners in March 2026 and started the way he starts with any client: an audit of each partner's technology, delivered in April with recorded walkthroughs. Since then he has built and run the infrastructure the team works on and the connectors that let its agents work inside it. He describes his role as technology strategy, product and infrastructure: the team spots the opportunity, he builds it, Jesse tests it and Jimmy tells the story. When he reviewed Common Ground's own project record in September he caught a compliance error before it spread: a self-hosted workflow tool does not sign a business associate agreement; the company hosting it does.

Also on his list

  • A finance and document automation stack, read-only inside the client's systems, proven on Common Ground's own books first.
  • Cascade IR, an investor-materials engine built with Jesse as a proof of concept on fictional data.
  • The security and tenant architecture memo Common Ground hands to client security teams.
  • AI adoption trainings for architecture firms, construction companies, nonprofits and an airline.

Zen Aegis on record

Robby founded Zen Aegis in 2023 and leads it. Its products, its client work (each client described by role, never by name) and the decisions behind them are on record here.

  • Foyer Hall
  • Slipstream scoring engine
  • Aegis Lens
  • Guardrails for a self-hosted agent platform
  • Email operations that learn from corrections
  • Grant Match AI
  • Four apps in one day
  • Cascade IR
  • Lifted Trucks mission control (prototype)
  • Medical-record review for an in-house legal team
  • Agent team for a multi-market business brokerage
  • Go-to-market build for a B2B SaaS company
  • Expert program for an online education company
  • Search build for an independent financial advisory practice
  • Sites for a strategy firm, a youth sports nonprofit and a family foundation
  • Story: Testing the engine against an expert before trusting its scores
  • Story: Keeping the prompts inside the walls
  • Story: A gate that will not let an unsourced claim out the door
  • Story: Two hours to fix the first client invoice
  • Story: Four apps in one day, built where people could watch
  • Story: No savings number before the baseline
  • Story: Collecting the facts instead of asking for them
  • Story: Building it instead of pitching it
